ei.title: Diya pointed at the lake and shouted, "Come on, Ryanna!"

fullPassage: Diya pointed at the lake and shouted, "Come on, Ryanna!" Ryanna stood still. She was wearing her regular clothes — her bathing suit was still in her bag. Her chest felt tight, and her hands were trembling. She didn't want to jump in. Something about it filled her with dread, even if she couldn't explain it. The thought of stepping into cold water with all her clothes on made her stomach twist. She looked at the adults standing on the dock, hoping someone would say, "It's okay. You don't have to." But no one did. They just stood there, watching. Her heart beat faster. She felt like crying, but she didn't want anyone to see. Especially not Diya. Everyone was looking at her now, and it made her feel even worse. She wanted to run away, but she felt trapped, like the fear had frozen her.

det.korean: ③ were → was. 주어 bathing suit는 단수명사이므로 단수 동사 was가 와야 합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① shouted: 과거형 → 적절
✅ ② stood: stand의 과거형 → 적절
❌ ④ were → was: 주어 'her bathing suit'는 단수이므로 단수 be동사 was 필요.
✅ ③ felt: feel의 과거형 → 적절
det.tip: 주어-동사 수일치: 단수(suit) + 단수 동사(was)

det.korean: ③ twisting → twist. 사역동사 made의 목적격 보어는 동사원형.
det.analysis:
✅ ① couldn't: 조동사 과거 부정형 → 적절
✅ ② stepping: 전치사 of + 동명사 → 적절
❌ ③ twisting → twist: make + 목적어 + 동사원형. make her stomach twist.
✅ ④ standing: 명사 adults 수식 현재분사 → 적절
det.tip: 사역동사 make + O + 동사원형. 현재분사/과거분사는 안 됨.

det.korean: ④ trapping → trapped. 주어가 '갇힌 느낌을 받는' 수동 상태이므로 과거분사 trapped가 와야 합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① hoping: 분사구문(능동) → 적절
✅ ② worse: even + 비교급 → 적절
✅ ③ to run: want + to부정사 → 적절
❌ ④ trapping → trapped: 주어 she가 '갇힌' 수동 상태. felt + 과거분사 = ~한 느낌이 들다. trapping(능동: 가두는)은 부적절.
det.tip: feel + 과거분사(수동): felt trapped(갇힌 느낌), felt trapped(가두는 ✗)

det.korean: ③ emptied(비웠다) → filled(가득 채웠다). 공포로 '가득 채웠다'는 원문과 반대.
det.analysis:
✅ ① tight: 답답한 → 적절
✅ ② trembling: 떨리는 → 적절
❌ ③ emptied → filled: fill A with B = A를 B로 채우다가 원문. emptied는 반대 뜻.
✅ ④ dock: 선착장 → 적절
det.tip: fill(채우다) ↔ empty(비우다). fill A with dread = A를 공포로 채우다

questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: cold = 차가운. 차가운 물에 옷 입은 채 들어간다는 생각이 속을 뒤틀리게 만듬.
det.analysis:
✅ ② cold: 차가운 — 원문 'stepping into cold water'와 일치
❌ ① warm: 따뜻한 — 편안함 연상, 속 뒤틀림과 모순
❌ ③ clean: 깨끗한 — 문맥 무관
❌ ④ shallow: 얕은 — 깊이 언급 없음
det.tip: cold water = 차가운 물 (불쾌감, 공포 유발)

✅ ② permission to opt out: 빠져나갈 허락 — '괜찮아, 안 해도 돼'라는 말을 바라는 심리.

❌ ③ praise for her courage: 용기 칭찬 — 용기 없는 상황
❌ ④ advice on swimming: 수영 조언 — 상황 초점 아님
det.tip: opt out = 참여하지 않다, 빠지다. 'You don't have to'의 의미 함축

questions.passage: Diya pointed at the lake and shouted, "Come on, Ryanna!" Ryanna stood still. She was wearing her regular clothes — her bathing suit was still in her bag. Her chest felt tight, and her hands were trembling. She didn't want to jump in. Something about it filled her with dread, even if she couldn't explain it. The thought of stepping into cold water with all her clothes on made her stomach twist. She looked at the adults standing on the dock, hoping someone would say, "It's okay. You don't have to." But no one did. They just stood there, watching. Her heart beat faster. She felt like crying, but she didn't want anyone to see. Especially not Diya. Everyone was looking at her now, and it made her feel even worse. She wanted to run away, but she felt ____ like the fear had frozen her.
